# Tools

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-tools-doc.js from src/tools/definitions.ts. Do not edit by hand: run `npm run build && npm run docs:tools`. -->

The connector offers 115 tools: 47 that read and 68 that change the world. Each description below is the one your AI client receives.

- **Access**: *Write* tools change the world. They are refused unless `FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true`, and run one at a time, in the order they arrive.
- **Needs**: what the tool uses. *FoundryVTT connection*: the Socket.IO connection, always there. *Companion module*: the module running in the invisible GM session (`FOUNDRY_MODULE_BRIDGE_ENABLED=true`). *REST API module*: the separate module enabled by `FOUNDRY_API_KEY`. See [Configuration](configuration.md).

### `search_actors`

Search actors (player characters, NPCs) by name, optionally filtered by type. Returns a summary line per match: name, type, and the level and current/max hit points when the actor stores them at details.level and attributes.hp. Use when: checking whether an actor exists, or getting a quick roster. Do not use when: you already have the actorId and want more of that actor's values - use get_actor_details; or you need the actorId itself, which this tool does not print - read the foundry://actors resource, whose JSON lists up to the first 100 actors with their _id (not exhaustive in larger worlds).

Parameters:

- `query` (string, optional) — Search query for actor names
- `type` (string, optional) — Actor type filter (character, npc, etc.)
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum number of results to return
- `cursor` (string, optional) — Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page

### `get_actor_details`

Get details for one actor by id: type, and the level, current/max hit points, armour class and ability values the actor stores at details.level, attributes.hp, attributes.ac and abilities (a game system that stores them elsewhere shows fewer fields; get_actor_stats returns all of its data); no biography or description text is returned (the description line always reads "No description available."). Use when: you have an actorId and need its current values - notably as the read-before-write step for update_actor_attributes. For one token on a map, give sceneId + tokenId instead of actorId: an unlinked token (a copy of a creature with its own values) reports its own values, a linked token the values of its world actor. Do not use when: you only have a name - run search_actors first; or you need the ids of items the actor owns, which this tool does not return - get_actor_inventory lists them.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, optional) — The ID of the actor to retrieve (omit when giving sceneId + tokenId)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id of the token, required together with tokenId
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id: reads that token's own actor (base actor and the token's changes merged, for an unlinked token) instead of actorId

### `get_actor_inventory`

List an actor's owned items (equipment, features, abilities…) with full system data per item, unlike get_actor_details which only reports the actor's own top-level stats. Use when: checking what a character or NPC carries or knows before an action or a trade. For one token on a map, give sceneId + tokenId instead of actorId: an unlinked token lists its own items (those it inherits from its base actor and its own, without the ones removed from it), a linked token its world actor's. Do not use when: you only need the actor's own values - use get_actor_details.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, optional) — The ID of the actor whose inventory to list (omit when giving sceneId + tokenId)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id of the token, required together with tokenId
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id: lists the items of that token's own actor (base actor and the token's changes merged, for an unlinked token) instead of actorId

### `update_actor_attributes`

Update fields on an actor's system data. Patch keys are dot-paths into actor.system (e.g. "attributes.health.value", "resources.primary.value", "details.notes") and values are absolute target values, never relative deltas. If the actor stores a value at one of these paths, it is range-checked: attributes.hp.value against max + temp, spells.&lt;key>.value against the max of that entry, and attributes.exhaustion against 0-10 (0-6 when the data of the actor marks older rules). Returns the post-update value for every patched path. Use when: applying damage or healing, spending a resource, or adjusting a stored value on a known actorId. For one token on a map - an unlinked copy of a creature, which has its own values - give sceneId + tokenId instead of actorId: only that token changes, not the base actor or its other copies. Write only stored fields: a field the game system computes from others is accepted and saved by the server, but has no effect in play. Do not use when: changing an item the actor owns (use update_actor_item) or only reading current values (use get_actor_details). WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, optional) — The ID of the actor to update (omit when giving sceneId + tokenId)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id of the token to update, required together with tokenId
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id: updates that token's own actor (its delta, for an unlinked token) instead of actorId
- `patch` (object, required) — Map of dot-path → value, where each dot-path addresses a field under actor.system (e.g. {"attributes.health.value": 30, "resources.primary.value": 2}). Values must be number, string, or boolean.

### `create_world_actor`

Create a new top-level Actor document (a permanent NPC or character sheet in the sidebar), optionally seeded with system data and filed under a folder. Use when: a new NPC or creature needs to exist as a persistent document, not just described in text. Do not use when: a quick throwaway description is enough - use generate_npc; or when adding an item to an actor that already exists - use create_actor_item. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Actor display name
- `type` (string, required) — Game-system actor type (e.g. "character", "npc")
- `system` (object, optional) — Optional system-specific data merged into actor.system
- `folder` (string, optional) — Optional Folder document id to file the actor under
- `flags` (object, optional) — Optional module flags for actor.flags, keyed by module id, e.g. {"my-module": {"key": "value"}} for data a module reads from the new actor

### `create_full_actor`

Create a new top-level Actor document AND seed it with starting items (gear, weapons, features, …) in one call, instead of create_world_actor followed by one create_actor_item per item. Pairs with get_document_schema: call that once per Actor/Item type to learn the real field names for `system`, then build the whole character here in a single call. The actor is always created first - a failure there aborts the whole call. Item creation is best-effort per item, not atomic: a bad item (e.g. a typo'd type) is reported in the response's item-failures list rather than losing the actor or the items that did succeed. Use when: standing up a fully-statted PC or NPC (correct attributes plus starting equipment and features) in one round trip. Do not use when: the actor already exists - use create_actor_item to add items to it; or a bare/generic actor is enough - use create_world_actor. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Actor display name
- `type` (string, required) — Game-system actor type (e.g. "character", "npc")
- `system` (object, optional) — Optional system-specific data merged into actor.system - use get_document_schema("Actor", type) to learn the real field names first
- `folder` (string, optional) — Optional Folder document id to file the actor under
- `items` (array of object, optional) — Optional starting items (weapons, gear, features, …) to create on the actor immediately after it exists

### `delete_world_actor`

Permanently delete a top-level Actor document. Use when: the user explicitly asks to remove an NPC or character sheet, and has given you the actorId. Do not use when: only removing a token placed on a scene - use delete_token; the actor document is untouched by that. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, required) — The ID of the actor to delete

### `search_items`

Search item documents in the world by name, optionally filtered by type. Returns name, type and rarity per match (rarity shows "Common" when the system records none); price is not available and always prints "Unknown price", and the rarity filter is ignored unless the REST API module is configured (FOUNDRY_API_KEY). Item ids are not printed - read the foundry://items resource, whose JSON lists up to the first 100 items with their _id (not exhaustive in larger worlds). Use when: checking whether an item exists in the world. Do not use when: searching compendium packs (use search_compendium) or listing what one actor carries (this searches world items, not owned items).

Parameters:

- `query` (string, optional) — Search query for item names
- `type` (string, optional) — Item type filter (weapon, armor, consumable, etc.)
- `rarity` (string, optional) — Item rarity filter (common, uncommon, rare, etc.). Applied only in REST API mode (FOUNDRY_API_KEY); ignored on the default Socket.IO path.
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum number of results to return
- `cursor` (string, optional) — Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response to fetch the next page

### `create_actor_item`

Create an item on an actor from an inline item document (type, name, system) or by referencing a compendium pack entry (compendium sources require the companion Foundry module). Use when: adding a new weapon, feature, or piece of equipment to a known actorId. For one token on a map, give sceneId + tokenId (an actorId given as well must be the actor of the token): an unlinked token gets the item on that token only, a linked token on its world actor. Do not use when: editing an item the actor already owns - use update_actor_item. Replacing an item is not atomic: create the replacement first and delete the old one second. Canonical target: D&D 5e v4+ activity schema. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, optional) — The ID of the actor to add the item to (omit when giving sceneId + tokenId)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id of the token, required together with tokenId
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id: adds the item to that token's own actor instead of actorId (only that token, for an unlinked token)
- `source` (object, required) — Item source. Either { type: "inline", item: { type, name, system } } or { type: "compendium", compendiumId, itemId } (requires companion module).

### `update_actor_item`

Apply a JSON merge patch to an item's system data on an actor: nested paths such as activities.{id}.consumption.targets are supported, values are absolute (arrays replace, null deletes). Use when: changing fields on an item the actor already owns, given actorId + itemId. For one token on a map, give sceneId + tokenId: on an unlinked token only that token changes, even for an item it inherits from its base actor. Do not use when: adding a new item (create_actor_item) or removing one (delete_actor_item). Canonical target: D&D 5e v4+ activity schema. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, optional) — The ID of the actor that owns the item (omit when giving sceneId + tokenId)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id of the token, required together with tokenId
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id: changes the item on that token's own actor instead of actorId (only that token, for an unlinked token)
- `itemId` (string, required) — The ID of the item to update
- `patch` (object, required) — JSON merge patch applied to item.system; nested paths supported (e.g. activities.{id}.consumption.targets)

### `delete_actor_item`

Permanently remove an item owned by an actor. Use when: the user explicitly asks to delete or discard a specific owned item, and you have its itemId from the user or from get_actor_inventory (which lists the ids of the items an actor owns) - never guess one. For one token on a map, give sceneId + tokenId: an unlinked token loses the item on that token only, even one it inherits from its base actor. Do not use when: only the item's data needs to change - use update_actor_item. In a replacement or migration flow, run create_actor_item first and this second: the two calls are not atomic, and failing after the delete loses the item. Echo the actorId and itemId back to the user and get their confirmation before calling. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, optional) — The ID of the actor that owns the item (omit when giving sceneId + tokenId)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id of the token, required together with tokenId
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id: deletes the item from that token's own actor instead of actorId (only that token, for an unlinked token)
- `itemId` (string, required) — The ID of the item to delete

### `create_actor_effect`

Create a general-purpose ActiveEffect on an actor with mechanical changes (attribute modifiers) and/or a duration - not just a status toggle (use apply_status_effect for that). Give actorId alone for a world actor, or actorId plus the sceneId+tokenId pair for one token: a linked token writes its world actor, an unlinked token only that token (its own copy of the actor), never the base actor or its other tokens. The token must carry actorId. changes[].mode is a named FoundryVTT ACTIVE_EFFECT_MODES combine rule (add/multiply/override/upgrade/downgrade/custom), not a raw number. Use when: applying a buff, a debuff, or an equipment bonus with a real mechanical effect. Do not use when: toggling a simple named condition (prone, stunned) - use apply_status_effect. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, required) — The actor's own document id
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id, required together with tokenId for an unlinked token actor
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id, required together with sceneId for an unlinked token actor
- `name` (string, required) — Effect display name
- `img` (string, optional) — Optional icon image path
- `description` (string, optional) — Optional effect description text
- `disabled` (boolean, optional) — Create the effect already disabled (default false)
- `statuses` (array of string, optional) — Optional status condition ids this effect also represents
- `duration` (object, optional) — Optional effect duration
- `changes` (array of object, optional) — Mechanical changes this effect applies

### `update_actor_effect`

Update fields on an existing ActiveEffect - every field replaces the corresponding one on the existing document, omitted fields are left as they are. Same actorId/sceneId+tokenId resolution as create_actor_effect: on an unlinked token only that token changes, even for an effect it inherits from its base actor. Use when: a buff's remaining duration changes, or its magnitude scales. Do not use when: the effect should end - use delete_actor_effect. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, required) — The actor's own document id
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id, required together with tokenId for an unlinked token actor
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id, required together with sceneId for an unlinked token actor
- `effectId` (string, required) — The ActiveEffect document id to update
- `name` (string, optional) — New effect display name
- `img` (string, optional) — New icon image path
- `description` (string, optional) — New effect description text
- `disabled` (boolean, optional) — Enable/disable the effect
- `statuses` (array of string, optional) — Replacement status condition ids
- `duration` (object, optional) — Replacement effect duration
- `changes` (array of object, optional) — Replacement mechanical changes

### `delete_actor_effect`

Delete an ActiveEffect from an actor. Same actorId/sceneId+tokenId resolution as create_actor_effect: on an unlinked token only that token loses the effect, even one it inherits from its base actor. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, required) — The actor's own document id
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id, required together with tokenId for an unlinked token actor
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id, required together with sceneId for an unlinked token actor
- `effectId` (string, required) — The ActiveEffect document id to delete

### `list_actor_effects`

List the ActiveEffects on an actor, read from the cached world snapshot (no socket round trip). Give actorId for a world actor, or sceneId + tokenId for one token: an unlinked token lists its own effects (those it inherits from its base actor and its own, without the ones removed from it), a linked token its world actor's. Use when: checking what buffs/debuffs are currently active on an actor before applying another.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, optional) — The actor's own document id (omit when giving sceneId + tokenId)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene id of the token, required together with tokenId
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token id: lists the effects of that token's own actor (base actor and the token's changes merged, for an unlinked token) instead of actorId

### `list_tokens`

List the Tokens placed on a scene (id, display name, linked actorId, x/y pixel position, width/height in grid cells, elevation, rotation, hidden, disposition), defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Read from cached worldData - no canvas access needed. Use when: you need to know what's on the map and where before moving, targeting, or applying an effect to a token, or to resolve a token's id from its name instead of asking the user. Do not use when: you need wall or tile layout instead - use list_walls/list_tiles.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `move_token`

Move a token to new x/y pixel coordinates on its scene; the token is located across scenes by id, optionally scoped with sceneId. Coordinates are absolute pixels, not grid squares and not offsets. Use when: repositioning a token to a position the user has given you, or one computed from list_tokens (current positions) and get_scene_info (grid size). Do not use when: repositioning several tokens at once - use move_tokens; or the destination may be blocked by a wall/door - use move_token_pathfind, which routes around them instead of teleporting through. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `tokenId` (string, required) — The ID of the token to move
- `x` (number, required) — Target x pixel coordinate on the scene
- `y` (number, required) — Target y pixel coordinate on the scene
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID to scope the token lookup

### `apply_status_effect`

Apply or remove a status condition (e.g. "prone", "stunned") on a token's actor. Set active=false to remove. Matches by status id, so re-applying or clearing-when-absent is a no-op. With the module bridge enabled, it first waits up to 10 s for the companion module if it is still connecting. With module 0.6.0 or later, the status goes through the game system's own status effects, so the system recognises the effect as its condition; effects carrying the status that were written earlier over the socket are reported when applying and removed with active=false. Some game systems ask for a value when a status is created; pass it in createOptions, under the option name the system documents. Without it, the call fails at once and nothing is created. createOptions need that path: they are refused when it is not available (no module 0.6.0, or writes disabled), and ignored when the status is already active. Otherwise, or if the module does not come, an effect carrying the status is written over the socket (its icon always shown), which a game system that defines its own statuses with fixed effect ids may not recognise. The answer names the path used. On an unlinked token only that token changes: a status it inherits from its base actor is found and can be removed from that token alone. Use when: a condition is gained or lost. Do not use when: changing numeric state such as hit points - use update_actor_attributes. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document. Exception: the no-op cases (applying an already-present status, or clearing an absent one) report success without attempting a write, so they also return normally while writes are disabled.

Parameters:

- `tokenId` (string, required) — The ID of the token whose actor to affect
- `statusId` (string, required) — The status condition id (e.g. 'prone', 'stunned', 'blinded')
- `active` (boolean, optional) — true to apply the effect (default), false to remove it
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID to scope the token lookup
- `createOptions` (object, optional) — Optional creation options the game system reads when a status is created (at most 10 keys, 1 KiB of JSON; not the core's own options such as parent or keepId). Only with active=true, through the companion module 0.6.0 or later

### `spawn_token`

Place a new token for an existing actor onto a scene at given x/y pixel coordinates, defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Base display fields (texture, size, vision) are seeded from the actor's prototypeToken. Use when: a creature, NPC, or reinforcement needs to appear on the map. Do not use when: repositioning a token that is already on the scene - use move_token. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, required) — The ID of the actor the new token represents
- `x` (number, required) — Target x pixel coordinate on the scene
- `y` (number, required) — Target y pixel coordinate on the scene
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene
- `name` (string, optional) — Optional display name override; defaults to the actor's name
- `hidden` (boolean, optional) — Optional; true to place the token hidden from players

### `delete_token`

Remove a token from a scene without deleting the underlying actor. Use when: a creature is defeated and removed from the battle, or a token was placed by mistake. Do not use when: the actor document itself should be deleted - use delete_world_actor; this only removes the token's placement on the map. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `tokenId` (string, required) — The ID of the token to remove
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID to scope the token lookup

### `move_token_pathfind`

Move a token to x/y coordinates, routing around impassable walls when the direct line is blocked (A* pathfinding over the scene's Wall geometry), and — unless openDoors is false — opening any closed doors the route needs to cross. Slower and more expensive than move_token (issues one document update per waypoint, with a short pause per door opened), and its wall detection covers ordinary geometric walls only, not anything canvas-only would also enforce (terrain height, drawing-based obstacles). Use when: a token should walk realistically around obstacles instead of teleporting through them, especially when doors are involved. Do not use when: the destination is in the open with nothing between - use move_token, which is one write instead of many. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `tokenId` (string, required) — The ID of the token to move
- `x` (number, required) — Target x pixel coordinate on the scene
- `y` (number, required) — Target y pixel coordinate on the scene
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID to scope the token lookup
- `openDoors` (boolean, optional) — Whether to open closed doors blocking the route (default true)

### `move_tokens`

Move several tokens in a single call - direct by default (like move_token), or wall-aware pathfinding per move when pathfind=true (like move_token_pathfind). Best-effort: one bad move (unknown tokenId, no route found, a rejected write) is reported in a failure list rather than losing moves that already succeeded. Use when: repositioning a whole party or group of NPCs at once - e.g. moving everyone into a room, or resetting an encounter's starting positions - instead of one move_token/move_token_pathfind call per token. Do not use when: moving a single token - move_token/move_token_pathfind is simpler. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `moves` (array of object, required) — One or more token moves to perform in this call

### `update_token_vision`

Update an existing placed token's vision and/or light emission properties (sight range, angle, vision mode, light dim/bright radii, color tint, angle, animation). WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `tokenId` (string, required) — The ID of the token to update
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID to scope the token lookup
- `sightEnabled` (boolean, optional) — Whether vision is enabled for this token (automatically set true if sightRange > 0)
- `sightRange` (number, optional) — Token vision range in grid units
- `sightAngle` (number, optional) — Vision cone angle in degrees (default 360)
- `visionMode` (string, optional) — Vision mode id (e.g. "basic", "darkvision")
- `lightDim` (number, optional) — Dim light emission radius in grid units
- `lightBright` (number, optional) — Bright light emission radius in grid units
- `lightColor` (string, optional) — Light emission color as a 6-digit hex string (e.g. "#ff8800")
- `lightAngle` (number, optional) — Light emission angle in degrees (default 360)
- `lightAnimationType` (string, optional) — Light animation type (e.g. "torch", "pulse", "chroma")

## Scenes

| Tool | Access | Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`get_scene_info`](#get_scene_info) | Read | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`create_scene`](#create_scene) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`switch_scene`](#switch_scene) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`delete_scene`](#delete_scene) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`set_scene_lighting`](#set_scene_lighting) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`reset_fog`](#reset_fog) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`set_scene_weather`](#set_scene_weather) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |

### `get_scene_info`

Get details of the active scene, or of a specific scene by id: name, scene id, active/navigation flags, pixel dimensions, padding, grid (type, size in pixels, distance, units), and lighting (global light, darkness); no description text is returned unless a module has set a description flag on the scene (the description line otherwise reads 'No description available.'). Use when: you need the sceneId, grid size, or the scene's pixel extents. Do not use when: looking a scene up by name (use search_world), or you need token/tile coordinates - this tool returns neither; use list_tiles or the foundry://scenes resource.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional scene ID. If not provided, returns current scene

### `create_scene`

Create a new Scene document from a background image already present under FoundryVTT's Data directory (see list_scene_assets to browse available map art). Width/height default to the image's real pixel dimensions read from disk (requires FOUNDRY_DATA_PATH) — the single biggest source of a misaligned grid when set by hand; pass width/height explicitly to override. Use when: a new location needs a scene before the party arrives there, or a fresh battlemap needs to exist as a document. Do not use when: the scene already exists - use switch_scene to activate it, or set_scene_lighting to change its lighting. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Scene display name
- `backgroundSrc` (string, required) — Data-relative path to the background image (e.g. "assets/maps/v1/x.jpg"), as returned by list_scene_assets
- `width` (number, optional) — Optional explicit pixel width; defaults to the image's real width
- `height` (number, optional) — Optional explicit pixel height; defaults to the image's real height
- `gridSize` (number, optional) — Grid cell size in pixels (default 100)
- `gridType` (number, optional) — Foundry grid type constant (default 1 = square)
- `gridDistance` (number, optional) — Real-world distance one grid cell represents (default 1)
- `gridUnits` (string, optional) — Unit label for gridDistance (e.g. "ft", "m") (default "ft")
- `padding` (number, optional) — Fractional canvas padding around the background image (default 0.25)
- `backgroundColor` (string, optional) — Hex color shown outside the background image (default "#999999")
- `activate` (boolean, optional) — Optional; true to immediately activate the new scene for all players

### `switch_scene`

Activate a scene, switching every connected player's canvas to it. FoundryVTT enforces a single active scene server-side, so activating one automatically deactivates whichever scene was active before - no separate deactivation call is needed. Use when: the party moves to a new map (new area, travel, a battle starting on a prepared map). Do not use when: you only need to read scene info - use get_scene_info. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, required) — The ID of the scene to activate

### `delete_scene`

Permanently delete a Scene document. Use when: the user explicitly asks to remove a map that is no longer needed. Do not use when: you only want to stop showing it to players - use switch_scene to activate a different one instead; deleting the active scene leaves no scene active. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, required) — The ID of the scene to delete

### `set_scene_lighting`

Set a scene's ambient darkness level (0-1) and/or global illumination fields (globalLight, globalLightThreshold). Plain Scene document fields - no canvas access required. Use when: transitioning to night, dimming a room, or lighting a torch-lit area. Do not use when: you only need to read current lighting - use get_scene_info. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, required) — The ID of the scene to update
- `darkness` (number, optional) — Ambient darkness level, 0 (fully lit) to 1 (pitch black)
- `globalLight` (boolean, optional) — Whether the whole scene is globally illuminated
- `globalLightThreshold` (number, optional) — Darkness level above which global light is suppressed

### `reset_fog`

Reset fog of war exploration progress for a scene, defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `set_scene_weather`

Set or clear weather effects on a scene (e.g. "rain", "snow", "leaves", "rainStorm", "fog", or empty string "" to clear). Default values come from Foundry core; additional effects may be available if weather modules are installed. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `weather` (string, required) — Weather effect key (e.g. "rain", "snow", "leaves", "rainStorm", "fog"), or "" to clear
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `list_walls`

List the Walls on a scene (id, endpoints, and the move/sight/door/ds fields), defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Read from cached worldData - no canvas access needed. Use when: finding a wallId for delete_wall/set_door_state, or checking a scene's current wall layout before adding more. Do not use when: you need tile or token positions instead - this only lists Wall documents.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `create_wall`

Create a new Wall segment on a scene - the structural building block for rooms, corridors, and doors. Unlike create_tile (which centres in a cell), a wall connects two grid *vertices* (intersections): fromCol/fromRow -> toCol/toRow, e.g. fromCol:3,fromRow:5 -> toCol:4,toRow:5 is the one-cell-long top edge of cell (3,5); a longer run spans multiple cells in one call. Alternatively pass explicit pixel x1/y1/x2/y2. type selects one of FoundryVTT's own named wall presets (the ones its wall-tool palette offers): "wall" (default, solid - blocks movement and sight), "door" (openable via set_door_state, starts closed), "secretDoor" (looks like a wall until discovered, starts closed), "terrain" (blocks movement; sight/light only block on the second crossing - hedges, foliage: you can see the hedge but not what is directly behind it), "invisible" (blocks movement but not sight - furniture, low obstacles, hidden traps), "ethereal" (the inverse of invisible: blocks sight but not movement - magical curtains, spectral barriers). Use when: building out a scene's room layout, or adding a door/terrain/invisible/ethereal wall to an existing wall line. Do not use when: you want to toggle an existing door open/closed/locked - use set_door_state; or decorate with a prop - use create_tile. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, required) — The ID of the scene to place the wall on
- `x1` (number, optional) — Start pixel x coordinate. Alternative to fromCol/fromRow.
- `y1` (number, optional) — Start pixel y coordinate. Alternative to fromCol/fromRow.
- `x2` (number, optional) — End pixel x coordinate. Alternative to toCol/toRow.
- `y2` (number, optional) — End pixel y coordinate. Alternative to toCol/toRow.
- `fromCol` (number, optional) — Start grid vertex column. Alternative to x1/y1.
- `fromRow` (number, optional) — Start grid vertex row. Alternative to x1/y1.
- `toCol` (number, optional) — End grid vertex column. Alternative to x2/y2.
- `toRow` (number, optional) — End grid vertex row. Alternative to x2/y2.
- `type` (one of `"wall"`, `"door"`, `"secretDoor"`, `"terrain"`, `"invisible"`, `"ethereal"`, optional) — Wall nature (default "wall"): wall = solid; door = openable, starts closed; secretDoor = hidden until discovered, starts closed; terrain = blocks movement, sight blocks only on the second crossing; invisible = blocks movement, not sight; ethereal = blocks sight, not movement

### `delete_wall`

Remove a Wall from a scene. Use when: undoing a placement mistake, or opening up a room by removing a wall segment entirely (as opposed to opening a door - use set_door_state to keep the wall and just toggle it). Do not use when: you want to remove a tile or token instead - this only affects Wall documents. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, required) — The ID of the scene the wall is on
- `wallId` (string, required) — The ID of the wall to remove

### `set_door_state`

Open, close, or lock a door (a Wall document with door !== 0). Use when: a party opens or shuts a door, or a door should be locked/unlocked. Do not use when: you don't have the wallId - use list_walls, or ask the user, or read the foundry://scenes resource. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `wallId` (string, required) — The ID of the door (Wall document) to change
- `state` (one of `0`, `1`, `2`, required) — 0 = closed, 1 = open, 2 = locked
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID to scope the wall lookup

### `list_scene_assets`

List image assets (map backgrounds, prop/token art) under a folder of the FoundryVTT Data directory, with real pixel dimensions and any `[Tag, Tag]`-bracketed keyword tags parsed out of the filename (the naming convention several battlemap packs use). Requires FOUNDRY_DATA_PATH — this server must run on the same host as FoundryVTT. Use when: choosing a background for create_scene, or browsing available decoration art for create_tile before placing anything. Do not use when: FOUNDRY_DATA_PATH is not set - this always returns empty in that case.

Parameters:

- `subdir` (string, optional) — Data-relative folder to scan (default "assets")
- `query` (string, optional) — Optional case-insensitive substring filter on filename or parsed tags
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum results to return (default 200)
- `kind` (one of `"image"`, `"audio"`, optional) — Asset category to scan for: "image" (default) or "audio"

### `list_tiles`

List the Tiles placed on a scene (id, image src, position, size, rotation, hidden), defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Read from cached worldData - no capture_scene screenshot needed to see current decoration state. Use when: checking what is already placed before adding more, or getting a tileId for delete_tile. Do not use when: you need token positions instead of tile positions - tiles and tokens are separate document types; this only lists tiles.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `find_open_cells`

Scan a scene's grid for cells with no wall crossing them and no existing tile/token already centred there - a placement candidate list for create_tile/spawn_token that needs no screenshot to compute. Restricted to the background image's own extent; the scene's padding margin is never returned as floor. Use when: deciding where to place a new tile or token without visual inspection. Do not use when: you already have a specific target position in mind - this is for open-ended 'somewhere sensible' placement, not for verifying one exact spot.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, required) — The ID of the scene to scan
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum open cells to return (default 50)

### `create_tile`

Place a decorative Tile on a scene from an image already present under FoundryVTT's Data directory (see list_scene_assets). Width/height default to the image's real pixel dimensions when not given. Position is either explicit pixel x/y (top-left corner) or a gridCol/gridRow cell (the tile is centred in that cell - see find_open_cells for candidates). By default refuses to place a tile whose bounding box crosses a scene wall; pass allowWallOverlap: true to place anyway (e.g. a wall-mounted prop). Use when: decorating a scene with scenery (crates, dumpsters, vehicles, graffiti) that is not a creature or NPC. Do not use when: the object is a creature/NPC that should have its own statistics and act in combat - use create_world_actor + spawn_token instead. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, required) — The ID of the scene to place the tile on
- `src` (string, required) — Data-relative path to the tile image, as returned by list_scene_assets
- `x` (number, optional) — Target top-left x pixel coordinate. Alternative to gridCol/gridRow.
- `y` (number, optional) — Target top-left y pixel coordinate. Alternative to gridCol/gridRow.
- `gridCol` (number, optional) — Grid column to centre the tile in. Alternative to x/y.
- `gridRow` (number, optional) — Grid row to centre the tile in. Alternative to x/y.
- `width` (number, optional) — Optional explicit pixel width; defaults to the image's real width
- `height` (number, optional) — Optional explicit pixel height; defaults to the image's real height
- `rotation` (number, optional) — Optional rotation in degrees (default 0)
- `elevation` (number, optional) — Optional elevation (default 0)
- `hidden` (boolean, optional) — Optional; true to place the tile hidden from players
- `allowWallOverlap` (boolean, optional) — Optional; true to allow placement even if the bounding box crosses a wall (default false - refuses)

### `delete_tile`

Remove a Tile from a scene. Use when: undoing a placement mistake, or clearing decoration that no longer fits the scene. Do not use when: you want to remove a token or actor instead - this only affects Tile documents; use delete_token or delete_world_actor. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, required) — The ID of the scene the tile is on
- `tileId` (string, required) — The ID of the tile to remove

### `list_lights`

List the AmbientLight sources placed on a scene (id, position, dim/bright radius, color, rotation, animation, hidden), defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Read from cached worldData - no canvas access needed. Use when: inspecting scene lighting or finding a lightId for update_light/delete_light.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `list_sounds`

List the AmbientSound sources placed on a scene (id, position, radius, audio path, volume, repeat, hidden), defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Read from cached worldData - no canvas access needed. Use when: inspecting ambient audio or finding a soundId for delete_sound.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `list_notes`

List the Map Notes (journal pins) placed on a scene (id, position, label text, linked journal entry and page, global visibility), defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Read from cached worldData - no canvas access needed. Use when: finding pins on the map or getting a noteId for delete_note.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `list_drawings`

List the Drawings placed on a scene (id, shape type, position, dimensions/radius, text label, colors, hidden, locked), defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Read from cached worldData - no canvas access needed. Use when: inspecting canvas shapes or finding a drawingId for delete_drawing.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `list_templates`

List the Measured Templates (area-of-effect shapes) placed on a scene (id, template type, position, distance, direction, angle, width, colors, hidden), defaulting to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. Read from cached worldData - no canvas access needed. Use when: inspecting active areas of effect or finding a templateId for delete_template.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `create_light`

Create a new AmbientLight source on a scene at either pixel x/y or a gridCol/gridRow cell (the light is centered in that cell). Supports dim/bright radii, color hex tint (#rrggbb), angle, rotation, and animation presets (e.g. torch, pulse, chroma). WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene
- `x` (number, optional) — Pixel x coordinate (center)
- `y` (number, optional) — Pixel y coordinate (center)
- `gridCol` (number, optional) — Grid column (centers in cell)
- `gridRow` (number, optional) — Grid row (centers in cell)
- `dim` (number, optional) — Dim light radius in grid units (default 0)
- `bright` (number, optional) — Bright light radius in grid units (default 0)
- `color` (string, optional) — Light color as a 6-digit hex string (e.g. "#ff8800")
- `angle` (number, optional) — Light emission angle in degrees (default 360)
- `rotation` (number, optional) — Light rotation in degrees (default 0)
- `animationType` (string, optional) — Optional animation type (e.g. "torch", "pulse", "chroma", "wave")
- `animationSpeed` (number, optional) — Animation speed 0-10 (default 5)
- `animationIntensity` (number, optional) — Animation intensity 1-10 (default 5)
- `walls` (boolean, optional) — Whether light is constrained by walls (default true)
- `vision` (boolean, optional) — Whether this light provides vision to tokens (default false)
- `hidden` (boolean, optional) — Whether the light source is hidden (default false)

### `update_light`

Update an existing AmbientLight source on a scene (radii, color, position, angle, animation, walls/vision/hidden). WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `lightId` (string, required) — The ID of the ambient light to update
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene
- `x` (number, optional) — New pixel x coordinate
- `y` (number, optional) — New pixel y coordinate
- `dim` (number, optional) — Dim light radius in grid units
- `bright` (number, optional) — Bright light radius in grid units
- `color` (string, optional) — Light color as a 6-digit hex string (e.g. "#ff8800")
- `angle` (number, optional) — Light emission angle in degrees
- `rotation` (number, optional) — Light rotation in degrees
- `walls` (boolean, optional) — Whether light is constrained by walls
- `vision` (boolean, optional) — Whether this light provides vision
- `hidden` (boolean, optional) — Whether the light source is hidden

### `delete_light`

Permanently remove an AmbientLight from a scene. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `lightId` (string, required) — The ID of the ambient light to delete
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `create_sound`

Create an AmbientSound source on a scene from an audio file path (browse available audio via list_scene_assets with kind="audio"). Placement is either pixel x/y or a gridCol/gridRow cell. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `path` (string, required) — Audio file path (e.g. "assets/audio/rain.mp3")
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene
- `x` (number, optional) — Pixel x coordinate (center)
- `y` (number, optional) — Pixel y coordinate (center)
- `gridCol` (number, optional) — Grid column (centers in cell)
- `gridRow` (number, optional) — Grid row (centers in cell)
- `radius` (number, optional) — Audible radius in grid units (default 0)
- `volume` (number, optional) — Playback volume 0.0 to 1.0 (default 0.5)
- `repeat` (boolean, optional) — Whether the audio loops continuously (default false)
- `walls` (boolean, optional) — Whether sound is blocked by walls (default true)
- `easing` (boolean, optional) — Whether volume fades towards the boundary (default true)
- `hidden` (boolean, optional) — Whether the sound is hidden/disabled (default false)

### `delete_sound`

Permanently remove an AmbientSound from a scene. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `soundId` (string, required) — The ID of the ambient sound to delete
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `create_note`

Place a Map Note (journal pin) on a scene at pixel x/y or a gridCol/gridRow cell. Must link to an entryId (journal entry), provide text (standalone label), or both. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene
- `entryId` (string, optional) — Optional JournalEntry document ID to link to this pin
- `pageId` (string, optional) — Optional JournalEntryPage ID within the linked entry
- `text` (string, optional) — Optional label text displayed below or on the pin
- `x` (number, optional) — Pixel x coordinate (center)
- `y` (number, optional) — Pixel y coordinate (center)
- `gridCol` (number, optional) — Grid column (centers in cell)
- `gridRow` (number, optional) — Grid row (centers in cell)
- `iconSize` (number, optional) — Pin icon size in pixels (minimum 32, default 40)
- `fontSize` (number, optional) — Label font size in pixels (8-128, default 32)
- `textAnchor` (number, optional) — Text anchor point: 0 (center), 1 (bottom/default), 2 (top), 3 (left), 4 (right)
- `global` (boolean, optional) — Whether the note is visible regardless of fog/vision (default false)

### `delete_note`

Permanently remove a Map Note pin from a scene (does not delete the linked journal entry). DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `noteId` (string, required) — The ID of the map note to delete
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `create_drawing`

Create a Drawing shape on a scene (rectangle "r", circle "c", ellipse "e", or polygon "p") with optional text, fill, and stroke styling. Position x, y is the top-left corner of the shape. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `x` (number, required) — Pixel x coordinate (top-left)
- `y` (number, required) — Pixel y coordinate (top-left)
- `shape` (one of `"r"`, `"c"`, `"e"`, `"p"`, optional) — Shape type: "r" (rectangle, default), "c" (circle), "e" (ellipse), "p" (polygon)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene
- `width` (number, optional) — Width in pixels (required for "r" and "e")
- `height` (number, optional) — Height in pixels (required for "r" and "e")
- `radius` (number, optional) — Radius in pixels (required for "c")
- `points` (array of number, optional) — Array of coordinates [x1, y1, x2, y2, ...] with at least 3 points (required for "p")
- `rotation` (number, optional) — Rotation in degrees (default 0)
- `strokeColor` (string, optional) — Stroke color as a 6-digit hex string (e.g. "#ffffff")
- `strokeWidth` (number, optional) — Stroke line width in pixels (default 8)
- `fillType` (one of `0`, `1`, `2`, optional) — Fill type: 0 (none), 1 (solid), 2 (pattern)
- `fillColor` (string, optional) — Fill color as a 6-digit hex string (e.g. "#336699")
- `fillAlpha` (number, optional) — Fill opacity 0.0 to 1.0 (default 0.5)
- `text` (string, optional) — Optional text label displayed inside the drawing
- `fontSize` (number, optional) — Font size in pixels (8-256, default 48)
- `hidden` (boolean, optional) — Whether the drawing is hidden from players (default false)
- `locked` (boolean, optional) — Whether the drawing is locked from interaction (default false)

### `delete_drawing`

Permanently remove a Drawing from a scene. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `drawingId` (string, required) — The ID of the drawing to delete
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `create_template`

Place a Measured Template (area-of-effect shape: "circle", "cone", "rect", "ray") on a scene at pixel x/y or a gridCol/gridRow cell. Distance is specified in scene grid units (e.g. metres or feet). WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `distance` (number, required) — Effect distance/radius in grid units (e.g. 6m or 30ft)
- `t` (one of `"circle"`, `"cone"`, `"rect"`, `"ray"`, optional) — Template type (default "circle")
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene
- `x` (number, optional) — Pixel x coordinate (origin point)
- `y` (number, optional) — Pixel y coordinate (origin point)
- `gridCol` (number, optional) — Grid column (centers origin in cell)
- `gridRow` (number, optional) — Grid row (centers origin in cell)
- `direction` (number, optional) — Direction angle in degrees (0 = right, 90 = down; required for cone/ray/rect)
- `angle` (number, optional) — Cone spread angle in degrees (required for cone, e.g. 45 or 53.13)
- `width` (number, optional) — Ray line width in grid units (required for ray)
- `borderColor` (string, optional) — Border color as a 6-digit hex string
- `fillColor` (string, optional) — Fill color as a 6-digit hex string
- `hidden` (boolean, optional) — Whether the template is hidden from players (default false)

### `delete_template`

Permanently remove a Measured Template area-of-effect shape from a scene. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `templateId` (string, required) — The ID of the measured template to delete
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene ID; defaults to the active scene

### `list_regions`

List the Scene Regions placed on a scene (FoundryVTT v12+). Regions are polygon/circle/rectangle areas that trigger behaviors when tokens enter, move through, or leave them. Use when: inspecting traps, teleport pads, atmospheric zones, or scripted triggers on a map.

Parameters:

- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional scene id; defaults to the currently active scene

### `create_region`

Create a new Scene Region with shapes and/or automated behaviors (FoundryVTT v12+). Shapes use pixel coordinates (use get_scene_info/find_open_cells to convert from grid cells). Documented behaviors include teleportToken ({ destination: &lt;region UUID> }), displayScrollingText ({ text, color, visibility }), adjustDarknessLevel ({ mode, modifier }), and pauseGame ({ once }); custom system/module behavior types pass through untouched. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Region display name
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional scene id; defaults to the currently active scene
- `color` (string, optional) — Optional 6-digit hex color for canvas rendering (e.g. "#ff8800")
- `visibility` (number, optional) — 0 = hidden from players, 1 = visible to players (default: 0)
- `elevation` (object, optional) — Optional 3D vertical bounds (null for unbounded)
- `shapes` (array of object, optional) — Pixel-coordinate geometric shapes defining the region boundary
- `behaviors` (array of object, optional) — Automated behaviors triggered when tokens interact with the region

### `delete_region`

Delete a Scene Region from a scene (FoundryVTT v12+). DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `regionId` (string, required) — The Region document id to delete
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional scene id; defaults to the currently active scene

## Combat

| Tool | Access | Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`get_combat_state`](#get_combat_state) | Read | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`next_turn`](#next_turn) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`end_combat`](#end_combat) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`set_initiative`](#set_initiative) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`start_combat`](#start_combat) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |

### `get_combat_state`

Get the active combat encounter: initiative order with each combatant's name and initiative, its hit points and armour class when its actor stores them at attributes.hp and attributes.ac, plus the current round and which combatant is up. Use when: reporting whose turn it is, or checking whether a combat is already running before start_combat. Do not use when: you need a combatantId for set_initiative - this prints names and ordinals, not ids; read the foundry://combat resource, whose JSON includes each combatant's _id and lists combatants in this same initiative order, so the Nth entry printed here is that resource's combatants[N-1] and combat.turn indexes it directly.

No parameters.

### `next_turn`

Advance the active combat to the next turn, wrapping to the next round after the last combatant. When skipDefeated is true, defeated combatants are skipped. Use when: the current combatant has finished their turn. Do not use when: only reporting the turn order - use get_combat_state. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `skipDefeated` (boolean, optional) — Skip combatants flagged as defeated when advancing. Defaults to the combat's skipDefeated setting, or false.

### `end_combat`

End the active combat encounter by deleting its Combat document, discarding the initiative order and round count. Use when: the fight is over and the user asks to end the encounter. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

No parameters.

### `set_initiative`

Set a combatant's initiative in the active combat (or in combatId when given), reordering the turn order. When that reorder moves the combatant who is currently acting to a different position, the encounter's turn index is rewritten to follow them - whoever was up stays up, and the result says so - rather than leaving the marker on whoever slid into the old slot. That follow-up applies only to the active combat: a combatId naming some other encounter still records the initiative, but its turn order is not readable here and is left alone. Use when: an initiative roll needs to be recorded or corrected for a known combatantId. Do not use when: simply moving on to the next combatant - use next_turn. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `combatantId` (string, required) — The ID of the combatant whose initiative to set
- `initiative` (number, required) — The initiative value to assign
- `combatId` (string, optional) — Optional Combat document ID; defaults to the active combat

### `start_combat`

Start a new combat encounter, seeding combatants from tokens: pass explicit tokenIds, or omit them to seed every token on the scene. Defaults to the active scene when sceneId is omitted. The encounter begins at round 1, turn 0, as when the GM clicks Begin Combat in Foundry. Use when: a fight begins and no combat is running. Do not use when: a combat is already active - check get_combat_state first, since this always creates an additional encounter. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `tokenIds` (array of string, optional) — Optional list of Token document IDs to add as combatants. Defaults to all tokens on the scene.
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional Scene document ID; defaults to the active scene.

## Journals

| Tool | Access | Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`search_journals`](#search_journals) | Read | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`get_journal`](#get_journal) | Read | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`create_journal_entry`](#create_journal_entry) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`update_journal_page`](#update_journal_page) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`add_journal_page`](#add_journal_page) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`update_journal_entry`](#update_journal_entry) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`delete_journal_entry`](#delete_journal_entry) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |

### `search_journals`

Search journal entries by name and page content. Use when: looking for notes, lore, or handouts by keyword. Do not use when: you already have the journalId - use get_journal.

Parameters:

- `query` (string, required) — Search query for journal names and content
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum number of results

### `get_journal`

Get one journal entry by id with the id and text of each page. By default page bodies are HTML-stripped and each is truncated to its first 500 characters, marked with a trailing "...", so long pages come back partial, and they come from the cached snapshot (flagged when it is stale). Pass raw: true to read the entry from the server instead, with the full, unmodified HTML and the version token of each page (version: &lt;token>) - the expectedVersion update_journal_page requires to replace the content of that page. Use when: you have a journalId and need the text of its pages, or a pageId and the exact current HTML before editing a page with update_journal_page. Do not use when: you only have a title or keyword - run search_journals first.

Parameters:

- `journalId` (string, required) — The ID of the journal entry to retrieve
- `raw` (boolean, optional) — Read the entry from the server and return each page's full, unmodified HTML (text.content) and version token instead of the stripped 500-character preview. Use before rewriting a page so no markup or text is lost, and pass the page's version to update_journal_page as expectedVersion.

### `create_journal_entry`

Create a new journal entry with one or more text pages, optionally filed under a folder. Defaults to GM-only visibility - pass visibility to let players read it. Use when: recording session notes, lore, or a handout in the world. Returns the id and version token of each created page. Do not use when: adding text to an existing entry - this always creates a new one. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Title of the journal entry
- `pages` (array of object, required) — One or more pages to create on the entry
- `folder` (string, optional) — Optional Folder document id to file the entry under
- `visibility` (one of `"gm-only"`, `"observer"`, `"owner"`, optional) — Who can see the entry. 'gm-only' (default) hides it from players; 'observer' lets every player read it; 'owner' lets every player read and edit it.

### `update_journal_page`

Edit one page of an existing journal entry. mode "replace" (default) sets a new name and/or replaces the whole page content; mode "append" adds HTML to the end of the page as currently stored on the server. Replacing content requires expectedVersion: read the page with get_journal raw: true, rewrite from that HTML, and pass the version printed for the page - the write is refused, with nothing written, if the page changed since. Every write saves the previous content to a local copy first, and returns the new version token so another edit can follow without re-reading. The response warns when the page looks open in a FoundryVTT editor, whose autosave can overwrite the write (FoundryVTT does not report an editor closing, so the warning can outlast it by a few minutes). Use when: correcting, rewriting, or extending session notes, lore, or a handout page. Do not use when: adding a separate new page - use add_journal_page; renaming or moving the entry itself - use update_journal_entry. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `journalId` (string, required) — The ID of the journal entry that holds the page
- `pageId` (string, required) — The ID of the page to edit (shown by get_journal)
- `mode` (one of `"replace"`, `"append"`, optional) — 'replace' (default) overwrites the page content with content (expectedVersion required) and/or renames it; 'append' adds content after the existing content as read from the server (name not allowed).
- `name` (string, optional) — New page title (replace mode only)
- `content` (string, optional) — Page body as HTML or plain text. In replace mode it replaces the entire page content; in append mode it is added at the end.
- `expectedVersion` (string, optional) — Version token of the page as last read (get_journal raw: true, or the version returned by the previous write). Required to replace content; optional in append mode. The write is refused if the page has changed since.

### `add_journal_page`

Add a new text page to an existing journal entry, placed after its last page as read from the server. Returns the new page id and version token. Use when: a journal needs another section (a new session, an NPC, a location). Do not use when: the entry does not exist yet - use create_journal_entry; changing an existing page - use update_journal_page. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `journalId` (string, required) — The ID of the journal entry to add the page to
- `name` (string, required) — Page title
- `content` (string, required) — Page body as HTML or plain text

### `update_journal_entry`

Rename a journal entry, move it into another folder, or change who can see it. Only the fields supplied change. Use when: retitling notes, filing them under a folder, or revealing a handout to players. Do not use when: changing page text - use update_journal_page; granting a specific user access - use set_document_ownership. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `journalId` (string, required) — The ID of the journal entry to update
- `name` (string, optional) — New title of the journal entry
- `folder` (string, optional) — Folder document id to move the entry into
- `visibility` (one of `"gm-only"`, `"observer"`, `"owner"`, optional) — Who can see the entry. 'gm-only' hides it from players; 'observer' lets every player read it; 'owner' lets every player read and edit it. Per-user ownership is kept.

### `delete_journal_entry`

Permanently delete a journal entry. Use when: the user explicitly asks to remove outdated notes or a handout. Do not use when: only the content, title, folder or visibility needs to change - use update_journal_page, add_journal_page or update_journal_entry instead. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `journalId` (string, required) — The ID of the journal entry to delete

## Chat and dice

| Tool | Access | Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`get_chat_messages`](#get_chat_messages) | Read | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`send_chat_message`](#send_chat_message) | Write | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`roll_dice`](#roll_dice) | Read | REST API module when a key is set, otherwise none |

### `get_chat_messages`

Get the most recent chat messages from the game log. Use when: you need recent in-game context - what players said, or roll results that already happened.

Parameters:

- `limit` (number, optional) — Number of messages to retrieve (default 20)

### `send_chat_message`

Post a message to the FoundryVTT chat log, optionally under a custom speaker name, whispered to specific users, and/or styled as out-of-character, in-character, or an emote (default: a plain system-style message). Use when: narrating a scene, speaking as an NPC, or sending a player a private clue. Do not use when: you only need to read recent chat - use get_chat_messages. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `content` (string, required) — Message body (HTML or plain text)
- `speaker` (string, optional) — Optional display name shown as the speaker (e.g. an NPC name)
- `whisperTo` (array of string, optional) — Optional list of User document ids to whisper the message to privately
- `style` (one of `"ooc"`, `"ic"`, `"emote"`, optional) — Message style. Omit for a plain message; 'ooc' out-of-character, 'ic' in-character, 'emote' an emote/action line.

### `roll_dice`

Roll dice and return the total with a per-term breakdown. Dice terms and whole numbers joined by + or -, with whitespace allowed anywhere ("1d20+5", "1d20 + 5", "1d20+5+3", "2d6 + 1d4", "3d6"; a count-less "d20" means one die), always work and every term counts towards the total - that is the portable grammar, safe on either transport. Multiplication and Foundry modifier syntax such as "4d6kh3" or "1d20r1" are rejected on both transports, with an error naming the offending character and its position, never dropped from the total in silence. Parentheses are the one difference: with FOUNDRY_API_KEY set the formula goes to FoundryVTT's own Roll engine, which evaluates them, while the default Socket.IO transport rolls locally and rejects them by name - and a REST roll that cannot reach the server falls back to that same local roller, so a parenthesised formula can still fail there. Prefer the expanded form when it matters. Use when: the user asks for a check, an attack, damage, or any random result.

Parameters:

- `formula` (string, required) — Dice formula (e.g., "1d20+5", "3d6")
- `reason` (string, optional) — Optional reason for the roll
