### `search_world`

Search across all collections (actors, items, scenes, journals) by name, grouped by collection. Use when: you do not know which collection holds what you are looking for. Do not use when: you already know the collection - use search_actors, search_items, or search_journals. Of those, only search_journals prints document ids; for actor and item ids read the foundry://actors and foundry://items resources, each of which lists up to the first 100 documents (not exhaustive in larger worlds).

Parameters:

- `query` (string, required) — Search query to match against entity names
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum results per collection (default 5)

### `get_world_summary`

Get world metadata (title, game system, core version) and per-collection document counts. Use when: orienting yourself in an unfamiliar world, or confirming the game system before system-specific edits.

No parameters.

### `refresh_world_data`

Force a re-fetch of the cached world data from the FoundryVTT server. Reads are normally served from a cache that follows live document changes for as long as the connection holds, so this is rarely needed. When the connection drops and comes back with the same session, the world is reloaded on its own in the background. Use when: get_health_status still flags the cache as stale (that reload failed, or changes arrived too fast to replay); or a read still looks stale after an out-of-band change. Refreshes the cache only; it does not modify the world.

No parameters.

### `list_folders`

List sidebar folders in the world (id, name, document type, parent folder id, color), optionally filtered by document type (Actor, Item, Scene, JournalEntry, Playlist, RollTable, Cards, Macro, Compendium).

Parameters:

- `type` (string, optional) — Optional document type filter (e.g. "Actor", "JournalEntry", "Item")

### `list_macros`

List Macro documents in the world (id, name, type script/chat, scope, folder, command preview). Use when: discovering available macros or finding a macroId for delete_macro.

No parameters.

### `list_playlists`

List Audio Playlists in the world (id, name, playing state, mode sequential/shuffle/simultaneous, channel, sound track list). Use when: checking background music/ambience state or getting ids for set_playlist_state.

No parameters.

### `create_folder`

Create a new sidebar Folder document to organize actors, items, scenes, journals, playlists, tables, or macros. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Folder display name
- `type` (string, required) — Document type this folder contains: "Actor", "Item", "Scene", "JournalEntry", "Playlist", "RollTable", "Cards", "Macro", or "Compendium"
- `parent` (string, optional) — Optional parent Folder ID for nested folder hierarchies
- `color` (string, optional) — Optional folder color as a 6-digit hex string (e.g. "#ff0000")
- `sorting` (one of `"a"`, `"m"`, optional) — Sorting mode: "a" (alphabetical, default) or "m" (manual)

### `create_macro`

Create a new Macro document (script or chat). Authors and manages the document only — this server has no tool that executes a macro (deliberate security boundary: no arbitrary JS execution in GM browser). WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Macro display name
- `type` (one of `"script"`, `"chat"`, required) — Macro type: "script" (JavaScript) or "chat" (chat command)
- `command` (string, required) — Macro command content/script body
- `folder` (string, optional) — Optional Folder ID to file the macro under
- `img` (string, optional) — Optional icon image path
- `scope` (one of `"global"`, `"actors"`, `"actor"`, optional) — Macro execution scope (default "global")

### `delete_macro`

Permanently delete a Macro document from the world. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `macroId` (string, required) — The ID of the macro to delete

### `create_playlist`

Create a new audio Playlist document with optional starting sound tracks. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Playlist display name
- `description` (string, optional) — Optional playlist description
- `mode` (one of `-1`, `0`, `1`, `2`, optional) — Playback mode: -1 (soundboard/disabled), 0 (sequential/default), 1 (shuffle), 2 (simultaneous)
- `channel` (one of `"music"`, `"environment"`, `"interface"`, optional) — Audio channel (default "music")
- `fade` (number, optional) — Fade duration in milliseconds
- `folder` (string, optional) — Optional Folder ID to file the playlist under
- `sounds` (array of object, optional) — Optional sound tracks to create on this playlist

### `set_playlist_state`

Start or stop playback of an entire playlist or a specific sound track within it. Drives Foundry playback state; client autoplay policies may affect audio output. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `playlistId` (string, required) — The ID of the playlist to control
- `playing` (boolean, required) — true to start playback, false to stop
- `soundId` (string, optional) — Optional PlaylistSound ID to control a specific track instead of the entire playlist

### `delete_playlist`

Permanently delete an audio Playlist document and its contained sounds. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `playlistId` (string, required) — The ID of the playlist to delete

### `set_document_ownership`

Configure granular ownership permissions for a document. entries maps user IDs (or "default" for all players) to permission levels: "none" (0), "limited" (1), "observer" (2), "owner" (3). Document types supported: Actor, Item, Scene, JournalEntry, RollTable, Macro. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `documentType` (one of `"Actor"`, `"Item"`, `"Scene"`, `"JournalEntry"`, `"RollTable"`, `"Macro"`, required) — Document collection the target lives in
- `documentId` (string, required) — 16-char alphanumeric document id
- `entries` (array of object, required) — List of target and ownership level mappings

### `list_roll_tables`

List the world's roll tables by name, result count, and id. Use when: you need a tableId for roll_table, or want to see what random tables are available. Do not use when: you already have the tableId - go straight to roll_table.

No parameters.

### `roll_table`

Draw a result from a roll table by id, rolling the table's own formula (or a uniform range when it has none) and returning the matched entry. This is a local, read-only draw: unlike FoundryVTT's own table draw, it does not mark the result as drawn or honor a no-duplicates setting, so repeat draws can repeat a result. Use when: rolling on a random encounter, loot, or event table. Do not use when: you don't have a tableId - run list_roll_tables first.

Parameters:

- `tableId` (string, required) — The ID of the roll table to draw from

### `create_roll_table`

Create a new RollTable document with text results. Automatically assigns sequential ranges and a matching 1dN formula when ranges are omitted. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `name` (string, required) — Roll table display name
- `results` (array of object, required) — List of text result entries for this table
- `description` (string, optional) — Optional table description
- `formula` (string, optional) — Optional custom dice formula (e.g. "1d100" or "2d6")
- `replacement` (boolean, optional) — Whether drawn results are replaced (default true)
- `displayRoll` (boolean, optional) — Whether the roll total is displayed in chat (default true)
- `folder` (string, optional) — Optional Folder ID to file the table under

### `delete_roll_table`

Permanently delete a RollTable document from the world. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `tableId` (string, required) — The ID of the roll table to delete

### `get_users`

List the world's users with their roles and online status. Online status is live while the Socket.IO connection is up: FoundryVTT's userActivity broadcasts are applied to the cached presence list as users connect and disconnect. It stops tracking while that connection is down - get_health_status shows the snapshot as stale until the world is reloaded, on its own once the connection comes back, or with refresh_world_data. Use when: you need to know which user holds the GM role, or who is connected right now.

No parameters.

### `set_user_role`

Change a user's permission role ("none", "player", "trusted", "assistant", "gamemaster"). Refuses self-demotion of the connected MCP user below assistant (3) to prevent accidental GM lockout. DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `userId` (string, required) — 16-char alphanumeric User document id
- `role` (one of `"none"`, `"player"`, `"trusted"`, `"assistant"`, `"gamemaster"`, required) — New role level for the user

### `get_world_setting`

Read a world setting by its namespaced key (e.g. "my-module.customSetting" or "simple-calendar.year"). If the setting has never been modified from its system/module default, exists will be false. Use when: inspecting world configuration.

Parameters:

- `key` (string, required) — The namespaced setting key in the format {scope}.{field}

### `set_world_setting`

Update or create a world setting value for a system or module namespace (e.g. "my-module.settingName"). Refuses writes to the "core.*" namespace (core settings control the Foundry client itself and can break the world; change those in the UI). DESTRUCTIVE and not undoable from this server: confirm the exact target with the user before calling. WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `key` (string, required) — The namespaced setting key in the format {scope}.{field} (non-core only)
- `value` (any, required) — The value to store (JSON-serializable: string, number, boolean, object, or array)

## Compendiums, rules and generators

| Tool | Access | Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`search_compendium`](#search_compendium) | Read | REST API module |
| [`generate_npc`](#generate_npc) | Read | None |
| [`generate_loot`](#generate_loot) | Read | None |
| [`lookup_rule`](#lookup_rule) | Read | FoundryVTT connection |

### `search_compendium`

Search FoundryVTT compendium packs by name and metadata; searches all enabled packs unless compendiumId scopes it to one pack. Use when: looking up creatures, items or rules that are not yet present in the world. Do not use when: the document already exists in the world - use search_items or search_world. Requires the REST API module (FOUNDRY_API_KEY); without it the search returns no results instead of failing.

Parameters:

- `query` (string, required) — Search query for compendium entry names
- `filters` (object, optional) — Optional metadata filters to narrow the search
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum number of results per page
- `cursor` (string, optional) — Opaque pagination cursor from a prior result's "Next page" cursor; omit for the first page

### `generate_npc`

Generate a random fantasy-style NPC as text, from built-in lists that do not depend on the game system of the world (name, people, profession, hit points, ability values, background). Use when: the user needs a throwaway NPC on the spot. Do not use when: the NPC must exist in FoundryVTT - this creates no documents, and the result still has to be entered into the world by hand.

Parameters:

- `level` (number, optional) — Character level (1-20)
- `race` (string, optional) — Character race (optional)
- `class` (string, optional) — Character class (optional)

### `generate_loot`

Generate random fantasy-style treasure for an encounter as text, from built-in tables that do not depend on the game system of the world. Only the coin amounts vary: they scale with challengeRating, while the item list is fixed (a healing potion and a silver ring) and the treasureType argument is accepted but not used. Use when: the user wants a quick coin total for an encounter. Do not use when: the loot should end up in an actor's inventory - this creates no documents; use create_actor_item for that.

Parameters:

- `challengeRating` (number, optional) — Difficulty of the encounter; the coin amounts scale with it
- `treasureType` (string, optional) — Type of treasure (hoard, individual, etc.). Accepted but not used - the generated result is the same whichever value is passed.

### `lookup_rule`

Search rules and mechanics across world journals and compendium journal packs. Compendium search requires the companion Foundry module.

Parameters:

- `query` (string, required) — Rule, keyword, or mechanic to look up

| Tool | Access | Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| [`search_compendium_content`](#search_compendium_content) | Read | Companion module |

| [`set_target`](#set_target) | Write | Companion module |
| [`get_actor_stats`](#get_actor_stats) | Read | FoundryVTT connection, companion module |

### `capture_scene`

Screenshot the active scene as seen on the GM's canvas, with a grid coordinate overlay (column,row per cell) burned in for spatial reasoning. Requires the companion Foundry module to be installed, enabled, and connected - fails with a clear error otherwise. Use when: you need to see the current map layout, token positions, or lighting to reason about it. Do not use when: you just need scene metadata (dimensions, darkness) - use get_scene_info, which needs no module.

No parameters.

### `get_document_schema`

Introspect the connected game system's real DataModel schema for an Actor or Item type - the exact field names, types, string-enum choices, and default values that type accepts, read live from the running system. Works with any installed game system. Returns a nested JSON tree: each field has `type` (Number/String/Boolean/Schema/Array/…), `required`, `choices` for constrained strings, and `initial` for its default value; `fields` holds nested sub-fields, `element` describes an array's entries; `persisted: false` marks a computed field that is never stored (writing it has no effect), and `min`, `max`, `integer` and `positive` bound numbers. A type the system declares only by template.json has no schema: the answer then lists its default values, with types inferred from them and marked `inferred: true` (module 0.6.0 or later). Requires the companion Foundry module to be installed, enabled, and connected - fails with a clear error otherwise. Use when: building a `system` payload for create_world_actor/create_actor_item/create_full_actor and you do not already know that type's exact field names - call this once per type, then reuse the answer. Do not use when: you already know the schema from a prior call in this session - re-querying wastes a round trip; the schema does not change during a session.

Parameters:

- `documentType` (one of `"Actor"`, `"Item"`, required) — Which document collection the type belongs to
- `type` (string, required) — The Actor or Item type to introspect (e.g. "character", "npc", "weapon") - system-specific; list valid types by trying an obviously-wrong one, or check get_world_summary/the system documentation

### `search_compendium_content`

Search compendium packs by name and journal entry text content using the browser-rendered Foundry session. Returns pack IDs, document IDs, names, and text snippet matches. Requires the companion Foundry module to be installed, enabled, and connected. Use when: looking up rules or items in compendiums.

Parameters:

- `query` (string, optional) — Text query to search for across pack names and journal contents
- `packType` (string, optional) — Optional document type to restrict search to (default "JournalEntry", e.g. "Item", "Actor")
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum number of results to return (default 20)

### `roll_and_post`

Evaluate a dice formula using Foundry's native Roll engine and post it directly to chat as a rendered, clickable roll card. Supports full Foundry dice syntax (e.g. "4d6kh3", "1d20r1", exploding dice) that the local parser rejects. Requires the companion Foundry module. WRITE: changes the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and the companion module, and is refused otherwise; FoundryVTT additionally enforces the GM permission.

Parameters:

- `formula` (string, required) — Dice formula to evaluate and post (e.g. "4d6kh3" or "2d6 + 5")
- `flavor` (string, optional) — Optional flavor/context text displayed above the roll card
- `speakerAlias` (string, optional) — Optional custom speaker alias displayed on the chat message
- `whisperTo` (array of string, optional) — Optional list of User IDs to whisper the roll to privately
- `rollMode` (one of `"publicroll"`, `"gmroll"`, `"blindroll"`, `"selfroll"`, optional) — Roll visibility mode (default "publicroll")

### `import_compendium_actor`

Import a compendium Actor (with its embedded items and effects) as a new top-level world Actor - the gap spawn_token cannot close alone, since it requires an actor that already exists in the world. Best-effort on embedded items: if the game system rejects embedded documents on create, the actor is recreated without them and each item is seeded individually, reporting per-item failures rather than losing the whole import. Requires the companion Foundry module. Use when: adding a creature or NPC from a compendium to the world before spawning its token. Do not use when: the actor already exists in the world - use spawn_token directly.WRITE: mutates the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and an active Socket.IO connection, and is refused otherwise; Foundry additionally enforces GM/owner permission on the document.

Parameters:

- `compendiumId` (string, required) — Compendium pack id the actor lives in (e.g. "world.creatures")
- `actorId` (string, required) — The compendium document's own id, as returned by search_compendium_content
- `folderId` (string, optional) — Optional 16-char Folder document id to file the new world actor under
- `name` (string, optional) — Optional rename for the world actor (default: the compendium name)

### `set_target`

Set or clear this GM user's target selection on the active canvas (renders the targeting reticle in connected player browsers). tokenIds are token document IDs on the currently viewed scene. Requires the companion Foundry module. Use when: directing player attention, declaring targets, or marking a shared target. WRITE: changes the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and the companion module, and is refused otherwise; FoundryVTT additionally enforces the GM permission.

Parameters:

- `tokenIds` (array of string, required) — List of Token IDs on the active canvas to target (or un-target)
- `targeted` (boolean, optional) — True to target, false to clear target on the given tokens (default: true)
- `replace` (boolean, optional) — True to release all existing targets before setting new ones (default: false)

### `get_actor_stats`

Read the actor's prepared system data, including values the system computes and does not store, as compact JSON. The cached world behind get_actor_details only holds stored data. Give actorId for a world actor, or sceneId + tokenId for one token on a map: a linked token reads its world actor, an unlinked token its own copy (base actor plus the token's changes). paths narrows the answer to some fields; an answer over maxBytes is refused with the size of each top-level key, so you can choose paths. Requires the companion Foundry module 0.6.0 or later. Use when: you need a value the game system derives (a maximum, a total, a modifier) or the current state of one token. Do not use when: you need items, effects or the stored source only - use get_actor_inventory, list_actor_effects or get_actor_details.

Parameters:

- `actorId` (string, optional) — The world actor's id. With sceneId + tokenId, optional: it must be the token's actor
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Scene of the token to read, together with tokenId
- `tokenId` (string, optional) — Token to read (an unlinked token has its own data), together with sceneId
- `paths` (array of string, optional) — Optional dot paths into system (a "system." prefix is accepted), at most 50. The answer then holds "values" keyed by path and the "missing" paths instead of the whole "system"
- `maxBytes` (number, optional) — Largest answer accepted, in bytes of compact JSON (default 32768, at most 65536)

### `get_targets`

List the current target selections of all connected users on the active canvas. Returns each user with the tokens they currently have targeted. Requires the companion Foundry module. Use when: checking who players are aiming at or focusing on.

No parameters.

### `ping_canvas`

Emit an animated canvas ping at specific pixel coordinates on the active scene's view, drawing every connected player's camera and attention to that exact location. Requires the companion Foundry module. Use when: pointing out a trap, landmark, or hidden detail on the map. WRITE: changes the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and the companion module, and is refused otherwise; FoundryVTT additionally enforces the GM permission.

Parameters:

- `x` (number, required) — Pixel x coordinate to ping
- `y` (number, required) — Pixel y coordinate to ping
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Optional scene id (fails if the GM canvas is viewing a different scene)

### `set_pause`

Pause or unpause the game clock. When paused, token movement and real-time combat timers freeze for players. Requires the companion Foundry module. Use when: stepping away, narrating a long cutscene, or resolving a complex rules question. WRITE: changes the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and the companion module, and is refused otherwise; FoundryVTT additionally enforces the GM permission.

Parameters:

- `paused` (boolean, optional) — True to pause, false to unpause (omit to toggle)

### `upload_asset`

Upload a file (image, audio, etc.) into FoundryVTT's Data storage via the GM browser's FilePicker, returning the Foundry-relative path to feed directly into create_scene (backgroundSrc), create_tile (src), or create_sound (path). Provide exactly one of contentBase64 (base64-encoded file content) or sourcePath (a file inside the folder named by FOUNDRY_UPLOAD_SOURCE_DIR, which the server reads; refused when that setting is unset). Only media files: .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .webp, .gif, .mp3, .ogg, .wav, .m4a, .webm, .mp4, and filename must have the source file's extension. targetDir is a folder relative to the Data storage (no "..", no absolute path) and filename a plain file name. Rejects files over 8 MiB. Requires the companion Foundry module. Use when: adding new map art, tokens, or audio the world does not already have. WRITE: changes the live world. Requires FOUNDRY_WRITE_ENABLED=true (default false) and the companion module, and is refused otherwise; FoundryVTT additionally enforces the GM permission.

Parameters:

- `targetDir` (string, required) — Destination folder relative to the Data storage (e.g. "assets/uploads"); no ".." and no absolute path
- `filename` (string, required) — Destination file name with a media extension (e.g. "map.png"), no folder
- `contentBase64` (string, optional) — Base64-encoded file content. Mutually exclusive with sourcePath.
- `sourcePath` (string, optional) — Path of a file inside the FOUNDRY_UPLOAD_SOURCE_DIR folder (refused when that setting is unset). Mutually exclusive with contentBase64.
- `mimeType` (string, optional) — Optional MIME type; must be the one of the filename extension, which is used when omitted

Exactly one of: `contentBase64`, `sourcePath`.

## Events and diagnostics

| Tool | Access | Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [`watch_events`](#watch_events) | Read | FoundryVTT connection |
| [`get_recent_logs`](#get_recent_logs) | Read | REST API module |
| [`search_logs`](#search_logs) | Read | REST API module |
| [`get_system_health`](#get_system_health) | Read | REST API module |
| [`diagnose_errors`](#diagnose_errors) | Read | REST API module |
| [`get_health_status`](#get_health_status) | Read | None |

### `watch_events`

Wait for and return world activity since a cursor - chat messages, token/actor/combat updates, door state changes, user connect/disconnect, and canvas targeting - instead of re-polling get_chat_messages/get_combat_state in a loop. Blocks for up to waitMs (default 25000, max 120000) if nothing has happened yet, returning as soon as something does; pass 0 to check without waiting. Your MCP client's own request timeout must exceed waitMs or the call will appear to fail while still running server-side. Always pass the returned nextCursor back as `cursor` on your next call - it is required to avoid missing or re-reading events, and a nonzero `dropped` count means events were evicted from the buffer before your cursor (increase FOUNDRY_EVENT_BUFFER_SIZE, or catch up with refresh_world_data/get_scene_info). Changing kinds/types/actions/sceneId mid-stream cannot recover events a previous filter already skipped past. Use when: waiting for a player to act, or checking what happened while you were doing something else. Do not use when: you need the full current state of something - use the matching get_*/search_* tool instead.

Parameters:

- `cursor` (string, optional) — "now" (default) to start from this moment, "oldest" for the full retained buffer, or a nextCursor value from a previous call
- `waitMs` (number, optional) — Milliseconds to block waiting for a new event before returning empty (default 25000, max 120000, 0 = return immediately)
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum events to return in one call (default 50, max 200)
- `kinds` (array of string, optional) — Restrict to these event kinds (default: all)
- `types` (array of string, optional) — Restrict to these document names, e.g. ["ChatMessage","Token","Combat"] (default: all)
- `actions` (array of string, optional) — Restrict to these actions, e.g. ["create","update"] (default: all)
- `sceneId` (string, optional) — Restrict to events on this scene (default: all scenes)
- `excludeSelf` (boolean, optional) — Drop events caused by this server's own account (default true). FoundryVTT does not send a client the broadcast of its own writes, so on v14 the connector's writes never reach the event log and false adds nothing for them; it still lets through changes saved by the same account elsewhere (the headless GM page, an editor open as that user).

### `get_recent_logs`

Get recent FoundryVTT server log entries, optionally filtered by level or since a timestamp. Use when: investigating an error or recent server behaviour. Do not use when: you have a specific term to look for - use search_logs. Requires the REST API module (FOUNDRY_API_KEY); fails without it.

Parameters:

- `limit` (number, optional) — Number of log entries to retrieve
- `level` (one of `"debug"`, `"info"`, `"warn"`, `"error"`, optional) — Log level filter (debug, info, warn, error)
- `since` (string, optional) — Get logs since this timestamp (ISO format)

### `search_logs`

Search the FoundryVTT server logs for a query string and list the matching entries. Use when: hunting a specific error message, stack trace, or module name. Do not use when: you just want the latest entries - use get_recent_logs. The reported match count is the server's total for the query, while limit caps how many of those entries are rendered (default 50, hard cap 1000). Level filtering accepts info, warn and error; "debug" is not a level this log store records, so it is reported back as unsupported and no level filter is applied. Requires the REST API module (FOUNDRY_API_KEY); fails without it.

Parameters:

- `query` (string, required) — Search query for log contents
- `level` (one of `"debug"`, `"info"`, `"warn"`, `"error"`, optional) — Log level filter; "debug" is not recorded by this log store and is not applied
- `limit` (number, optional) — Maximum number of matched entries to render (capped at 1000)

### `get_system_health`

Get the FoundryVTT server's health report: the overall status (healthy, warning, or critical), FoundryVTT and game-system versions, world id and uptime, active/total user counts with the number of GMs, active/installed module counts, connected clients, heap and RSS memory, and the log buffer size with recent error/warning counts and error rate. CPU and disk are not reported - the diagnostics response models no such fields - and the uptime and memory lines are omitted when the server does not supply them. Use when: you want the server's own view of its health. Do not use when: you also want connection and world status - use get_health_status. Requires the REST API module (FOUNDRY_API_KEY); fails without it.

No parameters.

### `diagnose_errors`

Retrieve error diagnosis and health analysis from the FoundryVTT server logs via the REST API module (FOUNDRY_API_KEY). Reports error categories, health score, actionable suggestions, and recent errors.

Parameters:

- `category` (string, optional) — Optional error category to filter summary and logs (e.g. "socket", "database")
- `timeframe` (number, optional) — Timeframe in seconds to analyze (default 3600)

### `get_health_status`

Get a combined health report: MCP-to-FoundryVTT connection state, world title/system/core version, and the server's health status with its active/total user counts, uptime, heap memory and recent error/warning counts. The world section is prefixed with a stale marker when the cached snapshot stopped following live document changes - typically a dropped connection, until the world is reloaded once it comes back (on its own, or with refresh_world_data). The connection line is a live read of the socket on the default Socket.IO transport, so it follows a link that drops or comes back in both directions; with FOUNDRY_API_KEY set there is no socket and it reports the outcome of the last REST request instead, not a live probe, so a server that went away between requests still reads as connected until the next request fails. Uptime and memory are omitted when the server does not report them; CPU, disk and playtime are not reported at all. Also lists the journal page overwrites detected in the last 24 hours (a connector write lost to a stale save or an open editor's autosave), with the path of each local copy. Degrades gracefully - sections that need the REST API module (FOUNDRY_API_KEY) report as unavailable rather than failing. Use when: first checking which world is loaded and whether the server reports itself healthy.

No parameters.
